sources.note: Peer-reviewed methodological study checked for why archaeological cultures cannot automatically be equated with bounded ethnic groups.

sources.title: Russian Archaeology, new evidence for Milograd agriculture
sources.note: Peer-reviewed article checked for chronology, querns, sickles, 44,517 pottery fragments, grain impressions, crop spectrum, weeds, sampling, and preservation limits.

sources.title: Institute of History, Academy of Sciences of Belarus, archaeology outline
sources.note: Academic synthesis checked for type-sites, settlement layouts, houses, storage pits, fortifications, burials, pottery, tools, and chronology.

sources.title: Institute of Archaeology, Academy of Sciences, Milograd synthesis
sources.note: Academic regional synthesis checked for settlement variation, houses, hearths, farming, animal remains, pottery, bronze work, ornaments, burials, and debated identity.

sources.title: Archaeology of Belarus, Milograd chapter
sources.note: Academic monograph checked for settlements, small houses, hearths, storage, pottery, iron and bronze working, exchange objects, graves, and transformation.

sources.title: Soviet Archaeology 1960, Milograd and Zarubintsy layers
sources.note: Institute of Archaeology journal study checked for stratified settlements, shared layouts, mixed deposits, storage-pit zones, and competing transition explanations.

sources.title: Archaeologia review, Milograd hillforts in Belarus
sources.note: National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine journal review checked for the scope, evidence base, and classification of Milograd hillfort research.

sources.title: Baltic Hillforts, Unknown Heritage
sources.note: Scholarly hillfort volume checked for Garoshkav topography, defensive works, scale, excavated remains, and comparative limits.

sources.title: Kyiv National University, early Slavic settlement and housing study
sources.note: University monograph checked for Milograd shallow-sunken houses, dimensions, central posts, open hearths, later architectural comparisons, and reconstruction cautions.

sources.title: NAS Ukraine journal, Rozvazh-Koshara settlement
sources.note: Peer-reviewed excavation report checked for 616 square metres, feature attribution, 65 Milograd sherds, ceramic homogeneity, chronological uncertainty, and cultural interaction.

sources.title: NAS Ukraine journal, Early Iron Age settlement at Kariv
sources.note: Peer-reviewed report checked for rare Milograd-style sherds west of the Styr and explicit uncertainty between exchange and human movement.

sources.title: Polish Academy of Sciences, horned spindle whorls
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study checked for Milograd parallels, spinning-tool forms, settlement and burial contexts, shared design traditions, and disputed functions.

sources.title: Institute of Archaeology RAS, horse-shaped pendants
sources.note: Peer-reviewed journal abstract checked for fourth-to-third-century BCE pendants across Milograd and neighboring archaeological cultures and workshop associations.

sources.title: Institute of Archaeology RAS, hillfort typology study
sources.note: Academic article checked for varied hillfort plans, areas, ramparts, ditches, landscape placement, cultural attribution, and empty or thin occupation layers.

sources.title: Eminak, Gremiachie cemetery attribution
sources.note: Peer-reviewed article checked for barrows, cremated human bone, handmade pottery, bronze pins, and uncertainty in cultural and chronological attribution.

sources.title: Lithuanian Archaeological Society, Palitskoje hillfort
sources.note: Excavation report checked for stratigraphy, handmade pottery, grain traces, animal bones, iron slag, mixed cultural forms, and the limits of small samples.

sources.title: Academy of Sciences early Iron Age settlement synthesis
sources.note: Academic book checked for Milograd settlement scale, houses, food remains, fishing evidence, iron tools, ornaments, and regional interactions.

sources.title: Western lands before Mongol Rus, archaeology and culture
sources.note: Academic synthesis checked for settlement placement, house types, querns, bone tools, craft evidence, and the history of social interpretations.

sources.title: Russian Archaeological Yearbook, Early Iron Age chronology
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chronological study checked for the Early Iron Age horizon in the forest zone and variation among Milograd dating schemes.

sources.title: National Mining University archive, Milograd settlement research
sources.note: Institutional archive copy checked for single-layer settlement context, fish evidence, burials, pottery, and explicit limits on interpretation.

sources.title: Polish Academy of Sciences, physicochemical pottery analysis
sources.note: Peer-reviewed methods study checked for macroscopic limits, raw-material analysis, forming, surface treatment, firing atmosphere, and cautious technological reconstruction.

sources.title: Historic England, Animal Bones and Archaeology
sources.note: Official professional guidance checked for recovery bias, identification, sampling, quantification, reporting, and differences between food waste, craft debris, and animal burial.

sources.title: Historic England, Archaeobotany
sources.note: Official archaeological science guidance checked for plant preservation, sampling, identification, food, fuel, medicine, craft, and environmental interpretation.

sources.title: Historic England, Wetland Heritage
sources.note: Official research guidance checked for waterlogged preservation of wood, leather, textiles, plants, settlement evidence, and threats to wetland sites.

sources.title: National Park Service, Benefits of Archeology
sources.note: Official archaeology explainer checked for stratigraphy, features, postholes, pits, privies, trash, flotation, mapping, context, and destructive excavation.

sources.title: Ohio State University linguistics, Neurians in Herodotus
sources.note: University classical-language resource checked for Herodotus references and the difference between a Greek ethnonym in a text and an archaeological attribution.

sources.title: Historic England, Human Osteoarchaeology
sources.note: Official specialist guidance checked for what skeletal evidence can reveal about health, diet, lifestyle, mortality, physique, and respectful treatment.

sources.title: Russian Archaeology, Milograd hillfort archaeobotanical collections
sources.note: Peer-reviewed article checked for grain-impression collections from three Milograd hillforts, crop identification, ceramic inclusions, chronology, and sample limits.

sources.title: Institute of Archaeology RAS, Milograd and Zarubintsy relations
sources.note: Recent academic study checked for round-bottomed bowls, Upper Dnieper stratigraphy, competing continuity and hiatus models, and continuing debate over the Milograd-to-Zarubintsy relationship.

sources.title: Vernadsky National Library, history of Milograd research
sources.note: National research-library article checked for discovery history, major excavations, corrections to mapped ranges, and twentieth-century Belarusian scholarship.

sources.title: American Antiquity, Archaeology as Anthropology
sources.note: Peer-reviewed methodological article checked for why similarities in one material class cannot explain every other cultural or social dimension.

proposedOverrides.name: Milograd archaeological culture
proposedOverrides.summary: Early Iron Age archaeological classification in parts of present-day Belarus and Ukraine, known through settlements, pottery, tools, farming evidence, and graves; its map dates and polygon are approximate.
